module_title: Major Soil Types in India - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) classifies Indian soils into 8 major groups based on their nature and characteristics. However, for competitive exams, mastering the top four most widespread soils—Alluvial, Black, Red, and Laterite—is your first priority.

core_concepts.title: Alluvial Soil
core_concepts.description: The most widespread and fertile soil in India (covering about 40% of the land). It is formed by the deposition of silt brought down by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers. It is highly suitable for growing wheat, rice, and sugarcane.

core_concepts.title: Black Soil
core_concepts.description: Formed from the weathering of volcanic rocks (basalt) in the Deccan Trap region. It is exceptionally good at retaining moisture. Found majorly in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.

core_concepts.title: Red and Yellow Soil
core_concepts.description: Develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall. The 'red' color comes from the diffusion of iron in the rock. It looks 'yellow' when it is in a hydrated form (contains water).

core_concepts.title: Laterite Soil
core_concepts.description: Found in areas experiencing high temperature and extremely high rainfall. The heavy rain washes away the topsoil nutrients (a process called leaching). With the right fertilizers, it is excellent for growing tea, coffee, and cashew nuts.

important_entities.name: Regur Soil
important_entities.key_fact: The local name for Black Soil
important_entities.significance: Black soil is internationally known as 'Tropical Chernozems', but in India, it is famously called 'Regur' or 'Black Cotton Soil' because it is ideal for cultivating cotton.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because it is found in areas with heavy rain and lush forests (like the Western Ghats), students assume Laterite is naturally highly fertile. It is NOT. Heavy rain 'washes away' the nutrients, making it acidic and naturally poor in fertility until manures are added.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct crop-to-soil matching is a staple question: Cotton = Black Soil. Cashew Nuts = Laterite Soil (especially in Kerala/Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh).
Remember that Alluvial soil dominates the Northern Plains and the Eastern Coastal Deltas.
